description: 4 exemplars + 2 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-17 because road-to-a-cold-start-paid-once step 2.6 touched this skill and brought it into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars cover the skill's own when-to-use list: an implementer with a judge, independent slices run in parallel, competing candidates, and the German phrasing of a parallel fan-out. Near-misses share the dispatch vocabulary but go to a different owner. One asks for a decision from external models, which the ai-council skill owns. The other asks for an isolated worktree with no orchestration, which using-git-worktrees owns. Counterexamples guard the 'agent' homonym in an unrelated sense and the 'parallel' homonym in test execution.

queries.q: implement this migration with one subagent and have a second one judge the diff before we apply it
these four bug fixes are independent — fan them out to subagents in parallel
have three subagents each draft a solution and pick the best one
verteil die unabhängigen Teilaufgaben auf parallele Subagenten und lass das Ergebnis prüfen
ask the external models for a second opinion on this roadmap
queries.note: a neutral opinion from providers outside the host session, not dispatch of host subagents → ai-council

queries.q: set up a separate worktree so I can try this refactor on the side
queries.note: isolation without any orchestration or judging → using-git-worktrees, even though one of this skill's modes uses worktrees

queries.q: update the user agent string our HTTP client sends
queries.note: the 'agent' homonym — an HTTP header, nothing to dispatch

queries.q: run the test suite in parallel to make CI faster
queries.note: the 'parallel' homonym — test-runner sharding, no subagents
